transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because of the bridges toward Miami. As soon as my car gets onto one of those long ones, my chest tightens and I grip the steering wheel hard. I suddenly feel like I have to get off right away, even though there’s nowhere to go.
Does this intense fear only happen when you are on bridges, or do you experience it in other situations as well?

It’s really the bridges, especially thinking about driving over all that open water. I know they’ve been there for years and people cross them every day, but the fear feels so much bigger than the actual danger.
How long have you been experiencing this intense fear of driving over bridges?
About 11 months now. It started when my daughter’s heart condition meant we had to make regular trips to see specialists in Miami.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient demonstrates an isolated, intense, and persistent fear triggered specifically by driving across bridges (situational specific phobia). Symptoms include physiological arousal (chest tightening, gripping the wheel) and an urge to escape, with insight that the fear is disproportionate to the actual risk. Symptoms have persisted for 11 months, well beyond the 6-month threshold.
